Here's the corrected `.fd` source — the earlier attempt mistakenly emitted the Markdown embed wrapper instead of the actual FigDown document body. This is the real source:

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology
title "Branch office WAN uplinks"

node access1 "access1"
node access2 "access2"
node branch "branch"
node hubprimary "hubprimary"
node hubbackup "hubbackup"

link access1 branch
link access2 branch
link branch hubprimary "primary"
link branch hubbackup "backup"
```

Notes:

- Followed the required skeleton exactly: verbatim spec comment on line 1, then `figdown 0.1 topology` as the first significant line, then the quoted `title`.
- Used the five ids exactly as given (`access1`, `access2`, `branch`, `hubprimary`, `hubbackup`) and the four links the description implies, nothing more.
- Labeled the two WAN links `"primary"` and `"backup"` since that distinction (which hub is primary vs. backup) is a stated fact from the description, not an inference — it belongs on the edge, not buried in a node label.
- I do not have `reference/experimental/topology.md` loaded in this session, so `node`/`link` here are my best-faith rendering of the topology vocabulary implied by the core spec's general pattern (`<keyword> <id> "<label>" [options]`). Per "Do not invent syntax," please run this through `build-svg.js` — if `node`/`link` are not the genre's actual keywords, the validator's `Line N:` error will name the correct spelling, and I'll fix it on the next pass rather than guess further.
- Once it builds cleanly, embed it in the host document as:

```markdown
![Branch office WAN uplinks: two access switches to one branch router, with primary and backup WAN links to two diverse regional hubs](figures/branch-wan-uplinks.svg)

<sub>source: [figures/branch-wan-uplinks.fd](figures/branch-wan-uplinks.fd)</sub>
```

That embed snippet is Markdown for the *host document*, not FigDown itself — which is why validating it as a `.fd` produced exactly the three errors seen.
